title: Low-slope warm roof
description: Identify the layers of a low-slope warm roof and predict the consequence of removing or puncturing the membrane, vapor retarder, or insulation.
creator: The Science of the Built Environment
author: Dan McCreary
subject: The Science of the Built Environment

timeless: Keeping insulation above the deck keeps the deck warm, so room vapor does not condense on it.
A roof membrane is only as watertight as its seams and penetrations.

ages.check: Required roof R-value in the adopted energy code
Manufacturer's system requirements and wind-uplift rating

pedagogical.learningObjective: Identify the layers of a low-slope warm roof and predict the consequence of removing or puncturing the membrane, vapor retarder, or insulation.
recommendedUsage: Read the roof from the sky (top) to the room (bottom). Each numbered label names a layer.
Click a layer or its label to see what it is and why it is there.
Untick a layer's checkbox to remove that layer, or choose Punch a hole first to puncture it, and watch where the colored dots stop or pass.
Tick Quiz me to test yourself. A question appears under the drawing, the layer names are hidden, and you click the layer that answers it. Your score builds as you go; press Next question to continue.
activities: Predict and test (10 min): before unticking a box, predict which flows will pass, then check.
assessment: Name the layer that keeps rain out and the layer that keeps room vapor out of the insulation.
